paragraphs: Airfoil inverse design starts with desired properties or changes and seeks a suitable shape. Generative models offer a promising way to do this, but building large public datasets is expensive. AFBench addresses that research bottleneck with a benchmark containing 200,000 airfoils, accompanied by labels describing their geometry and aerodynamic properties.

The benchmark defines two practical tasks: generating airfoils conditioned on physical parameters and editing existing designs with user control. Its emphasis on multiple kinds of instructions reflects the design problem described by the authors, where a user may specify physical requirements or manipulate points on a shape. Evaluation therefore needs to consider both geometric suitability and aerodynamic suitability.

AFBench also supplies evaluation metrics, baseline models, experimental observations, and analysis to support comparisons between methods. The authors report training their baseline on an RTX 3090 within 16 hours. The contribution is a shared foundation for developing and assessing controllable design methods, with the stated aim of connecting research ideas more closely to practical airfoil design.
neurips-2024-afbench-a-large-scale-bench.tldr: AFBench provides 200,000 labeled airfoils and shared tasks for evaluating conditional generation and controllable airfoil editing.

paragraphs: An AI agent that uses external tools must interpret material it did not create or control. Prompt injection exploits this situation: instructions embedded in returned data can redirect the agent toward an attacker's task. AgentDojo provides an environment for testing how reliably agents complete legitimate work while encountering this kind of untrusted information.

The environment includes 97 realistic tasks and 629 security test cases, covering activities such as email management, online banking, and travel booking. It also incorporates attack and defense approaches from existing research. Its extensible design allows researchers to introduce new tasks, defenses, and adaptive attacks as the security problem changes.

The evaluations reveal difficulties on both sides. Leading language models fail many legitimate tasks even without attacks, while existing injection attacks compromise some security properties but leave others intact. These findings make ordinary task competence part of the evaluation problem alongside resistance to manipulation. AgentDojo is intended to support research into agents that can satisfy both requirements more reliably.
neurips-2024-agentdojo-a-dynamic-environ.tldr: AgentDojo offers an extensible environment for testing tool-using agents against prompt injection while also measuring legitimate task performance.

paragraphs: Protecting dataset labels requires accounting for what an attacker could already infer from the available features. This paper proposes measuring how much access to privatized labels improves an attacker's ability to reconstruct true labels. The comparison attacker sees only feature vectors but may already know how features and labels are related.

The authors develop additive and multiplicative versions of this reconstruction advantage. Together, these measures encompass approaches used in empirical privacy auditing and differential privacy. They provide a common basis for comparing different protections, including aggregated labels, randomized noisy labels, and schemes that do not provide differential privacy.

The paper analyzes the measures under a distributional model that the authors argue captures reasonable adversarial settings. It also studies their behavior on real and simulated prediction tasks. Across the experimental settings examined, differentially private schemes match or outperform more heuristic methods in the tradeoff between privacy and usefulness. The result supports those schemes within the tested settings while grounding comparisons in additional information gained by an attacker.
neurips-2024-auditing-privacy-mechanisms.tldr: Reconstruction advantage measures compare label privacy schemes by the extra inference ability they give an attacker beyond the features alone.

paragraphs: Natural experiments require estimating treatment effects when treatment assignments already exist. Using a dataset from an early childhood literacy nonprofit, the authors find that more than 20 established estimators give inconsistent assessments of the program's effectiveness. That disagreement motivates a benchmark in which estimator accuracy can be evaluated more directly.

The benchmark combines the dataset with synthetic outcomes designed with guidance from domain experts. It varies conditions including sample size, relationships between treatments, and the accuracy of estimated treatment probabilities. In these comparisons, doubly robust estimators based on regression adjustment generally outperform more complicated alternatives by orders of magnitude.

The authors also derive a closed-form variance expression for doubly robust estimators that use dataset splitting to obtain unbiased estimates. This expression motivates a new loss function for fitting the regression adjustment components of a new estimator. A modular Python package makes the dataset and benchmark available for extension. The work connects an applied disagreement about treatment effects to controlled evaluation and a theoretically motivated algorithmic improvement.
neurips-2024-benchmarking-estimators-for.tldr: A natural-experiment benchmark favors doubly robust estimators and motivates a new estimator through an explicit variance analysis.

paragraphs: Neural architecture search can consume substantial energy while exploring and evaluating candidate models. CE-NAS targets the carbon emissions of that design process. Its approach accounts for both differences in the energy demands of search operations and variation in the carbon intensity of the energy used to power them.

A time-series transformer predicts carbon intensity, and a reinforcement learning agent uses that information to adjust GPU resources dynamically. The controller balances relatively economical sampling against more energy-intensive evaluation. A multi-objective optimizer further reduces the search space, combining decisions about which architectures to explore with decisions about how to allocate computation.

On HW-NasBench, the authors report carbon reductions of up to a factor of 7.22 while retaining search efficiency comparable to standard NAS. They also report strong results for open-domain searches on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet. These findings support treating resource allocation and carbon intensity as part of architecture search itself, alongside the performance of the model ultimately selected.
neurips-2024-ce-nas-an-end-to-end-carbon.tldr: CE-NAS combines carbon forecasts, adaptive GPU allocation, and search-space reduction to lower architecture-search emissions while retaining strong model performance.

paragraphs: A photorealistic avatar that someone can embody needs full-body coverage, the ability to follow the user's current motion and appearance, and adaptability to new identities. Codec Avatar Studio addresses the data requirements behind these goals. It provides paired captures of the same people using systems with different levels of quality and accessibility.

One dataset includes 256 subjects, pairing detailed multi-view head scans with video from cameras inside a headset. This collection targets generalization and the ability to drive an avatar from user observations. A second dataset covers four subjects in eight capture modalities, emphasizing more complete human modeling across heads, hands, and bodies.

The second collection includes relightable head and hand captures, full-body captures in minimal and regular clothing, and corresponding phone recordings. These pairings connect detailed reference captures with more accessible recording methods. The authors also provide code and pretrained human generation models. The contribution expands researcher access to paired data that the abstract describes as rarely available outside specialized industrial laboratories.
neurips-2024-codec-avatar-studio-paired-.tldr: Codec Avatar Studio provides paired human captures and models to support complete, controllable avatars that can adapt to new identities.

paragraphs: A pretrained vision-language model can help detect unfamiliar images by comparing them with labels for both known and potentially unknown categories. The choice of unknown-category labels is therefore important. This paper studies how expanding that candidate pool can improve zero-shot detection of inputs outside the intended distribution.

The analysis identifies three relevant requirements: a larger pool, a higher expected chance that unfamiliar images activate the selected labels, and low dependence between those activations. Simply adding dictionary words introduces synonyms and obscure terms that fail to satisfy these requirements. The authors instead construct a conjugated semantic pool using modified names of broad categories.

These descriptions serve as centers for groups of images that share properties across specific categories. Because the final decision distinguishes known from unknown inputs, useful candidates need not be conventional class names. The authors report that this expansion satisfies their theoretical requirements and improves FPR95 by 7.89% over existing work. The result highlights the structure and usefulness of label candidates, beyond the sheer size of their vocabulary.
neurips-2024-conjugated-semantic-pool-im.tldr: Modified broad-category descriptions improve zero-shot unfamiliar-image detection by expanding label candidates in a theoretically motivated way.

paragraphs: The same visual dataset can contain several meaningful ways to group its contents. Multiple clustering tries to uncover these different structures, but a collection of automatically discovered groupings may still require users to interpret which one fits their needs. Multi-Sub makes the user's requested perspective part of the clustering process.

The method combines CLIP and GPT-4 to connect text describing user preferences with visual representations. A language model automatically generates proxy words that serve as bases for a representation subspace. These words provide a way to express the data through concepts related to the user's interests, guiding how the visual information is represented for grouping.

This mechanism forms an end-to-end framework for customized multiple clustering. Across the visual clustering datasets studied, Multi-Sub consistently outperforms the existing baselines. The reported contribution is therefore both a method for communicating desired grouping criteria and evidence that incorporating those criteria through multimodal representations can improve clustering performance in the evaluated tasks.
neurips-2024-customized-multiple-cluster.tldr: Multi-Sub uses language-generated proxy words and vision-language representations to cluster images according to user preferences.

paragraphs: Disentangled representation learning aims to separate the underlying factors that explain observed data. Doing this without supervision is difficult, and many methods rely on specially designed losses or structures. This paper investigates whether the reconstruction process of a diffusion model with cross-attention can itself encourage that separation.

An encoder turns an image into a set of concept tokens. A latent diffusion model then uses these tokens as conditions while reconstructing the image, with cross-attention connecting the encoder's output to the diffusion U-Net. The authors analyze the diffusion process as providing information bottlenecks that change over time. Together with cross-attention, these bottlenecks encourage the model to learn separated representations.

The framework uses no additional regularization term in its loss and reports disentanglement results exceeding previous methods on the benchmark datasets studied. Ablation experiments and visualizations investigate how its components function. The findings suggest that the generative model's own information flow can provide a useful bias toward disentanglement, reducing reliance on elaborate loss designs in this setting.
neurips-2024-diffusion-model-with-cross-.tldr: A diffusion reconstruction model conditioned on concept tokens encourages disentangled representations through cross-attention and changing information bottlenecks.

paragraphs: Convolutional neural networks work well on array-shaped data, while biological and social networks have graph structure. Quantized Graph Convolution Networks aim to transfer CNN strengths to this less regular setting through a direct mathematical extension. A central requirement is that the proposed graph operation recovers a two-dimensional CNN layer when applied to array data.

The method divides convolution into non-overlapping sub-kernels and learns how to assign graph neighborhoods to them. Treating assignment as a learnable choice among multiple categories allows the framework to handle graphs of arbitrary size and dimension. This makes the organization of the neighborhood part of what the model learns.

The authors incorporate these operations into a residual network and evaluate them on graph benchmarks and a new finite element graph dataset for predicting nonlinear dynamics properties. Performance matches or exceeds the state-of-the-art graph networks used in those comparisons. The contribution combines a formal connection to ordinary convolution with empirical evidence that the resulting architecture is useful beyond regular grids.
neurips-2024-generalizing-cnns-to-graphs.tldr: QGCNs extend CNN convolution to graphs through learned sub-kernel assignments while recovering ordinary two-dimensional convolution on array data.

paragraphs: Latent diffusion models generate in a compact representation space and use a decoder to produce pixels. Some applications also need to invert that decoder accurately, but the accompanying encoder does not generally supply the exact inverse required. Previous inversion methods use gradients, which become expensive in memory and computation as the latent representation grows.

The paper proposes an inversion method that avoids gradient computation and applies across different latent models. It studies convergence for both a forward-step method and inertial Krasnoselskii-Mann iterations. The theoretical results rely on a mild cocoercivity assumption, which the authors state is satisfied by recent latent diffusion models.

The implemented approach combines gradient-free inversion with Adam and learning-rate scheduling. It substantially reduces computation time and memory use relative to earlier gradient-based methods while reaching comparable error levels. Demonstrated applications include watermarking in noise space and image editing that preserves backgrounds. The work addresses a practical constraint on accurate inversion, particularly relevant when larger latent spaces make gradient-based approaches difficult to run.
neurips-2024-gradient-free-decoder-inver.tldr: Gradient-free decoder inversion reduces memory and computation costs in latent diffusion models while achieving errors comparable to gradient-based methods.

paragraphs: Crowdsourced labels can be unreliable because annotators differ in expertise. Existing methods often estimate the probabilities of the true labels from each example and its noisy annotations. This paper addresses a further source of error: those estimated probabilities may themselves be misspecified, especially when annotation noise is high.

The authors formulate learning as conditional distributionally robust optimization. Instead of relying on one estimated label distribution, the objective considers the worst risk among distributions within a specified distance of a reference. Analysis of the corresponding dual problem provides risk bounds and an analytical expression for the robust risk associated with each example.

A robust pseudo-labeling procedure uses a likelihood-ratio test to construct the reference distribution. Additional closed-form results for empirical robust risk and the optimal dual multiplier make the optimization more efficient and give a principled way to balance robustness with fitting the data. Experiments on synthetic and real datasets report superior performance, supporting explicit treatment of uncertainty in the estimated true-label probabilities.
neurips-2024-learning-from-noisy-labels-.tldr: The method learns from noisy annotations by optimizing against uncertainty around estimated true-label distributions and constructing robust pseudo-labels.

paragraphs: Unsupervised reinforcement learning can use internally generated rewards to explore and acquire general skills. With visual observations, however, distracting changes can distort those rewards and pull exploration away from useful aspects of the environment. SeeX addresses this problem by separating information within the world model used to guide exploration.

The framework has two linked optimization levels. The inner level trains a world model that distinguishes exogenous and endogenous information, minimizing uncertainty to support task relevance. The outer level trains a policy using imagined trajectories generated in the endogenous state space. Within that space, the policy seeks to maximize uncertainty relevant to the task.

These two objectives serve different purposes: learning the separation helps identify the information that should guide exploration, while policy learning seeks informative experiences within that representation. Evaluations on several locomotion and manipulation tasks demonstrate the method's effectiveness. The findings support using a separated world model to make uncertainty-driven exploration more useful when image or video observations contain distracting variation.
neurips-2024-leveraging-separated-world-.tldr: SeeX separates world-model information so exploration can target task-relevant uncertainty despite visual distractions.

paragraphs: This paper studies how prediction error decreases with additional data for regularized learning algorithms whose outputs are vectors. The analyzed family includes kernel ridge regression, kernel principal component regression, and several forms of gradient descent. Its scope also includes outputs with infinitely many dimensions, extending the theory beyond ordinary finite-dimensional prediction.

The first result establishes a saturation effect for vector-valued ridge regression. A new lower bound shows that when the target regression function becomes smoother than a certain level, ridge regression has a suboptimal learning rate. Thus, additional smoothness does not necessarily translate into an optimally faster rate for this particular method.

The second result bounds finite-sample risk for the broader family of spectral algorithms. It covers both targets inside the hypothesis space and misspecified cases where the true function lies outside it. In several regimes, the bound is minimax optimal, matching the best worst-case rate available for the problem class. Together, the results distinguish a limitation of ridge regression from stronger guarantees available across the wider algorithm family.
neurips-2024-optimal-rates-for-vector-va.tldr: The paper proves ridge-regression saturation and establishes minimax-optimal risk bounds in several regimes for vector-valued spectral learning algorithms.

paragraphs: Multi-view representation learning combines different views of the same object into a unified representation. Deep Canonical Correlation Analysis and related methods perform strongly, but the authors observe a serious training instability: performance can deteriorate sharply as training continues. This collapse makes deciding when to stop training particularly consequential and difficult.

The proposed NR-DCCA adds noise regularization to prevent that failure. The theoretical analysis identifies a Correlation Invariant Property as central to avoiding collapse and shows that the regularization forces the network to possess it. The method therefore ties a change in training to a specific property implicated in stability.

The authors also create synthetic datasets with adjustable amounts of information shared across views and information that complements other views. These datasets support broader comparisons of multi-view methods. NR-DCCA consistently and stably outperforms baselines on both synthetic and real-world data. The regularization can also extend to other DCCA-based methods, including DGCCA, suggesting that its usefulness reaches beyond the single proposed model.
neurips-2024-preventing-model-collapse-i.tldr: NR-DCCA uses theoretically motivated noise regularization to prevent training collapse and improve multi-view representation learning.

paragraphs: Diffusion models learn denoising information that can represent a prior over realistic data. In inverse problems, posterior sampling combines that prior with measurements to generate plausible underlying signals. This paper studies when such sampling can have quantitative guarantees, addressing a gap left by heuristic approaches used for this purpose.

The authors first establish a hardness result: a generic procedure using only the prior denoising oracle becomes infeasible when the measurement operator is even mildly ill-conditioned. They then introduce tilted transport for linear inverse problems. It combines the quadratic structure of the log-likelihood with the denoising oracle to transform the original posterior problem exactly into an easier sampling problem.

The analysis gives conditions under which the transformed posterior is strongly log-concave, a property useful for sampling guarantees. Those conditions expose how difficulty depends on measurement conditioning and signal-to-noise ratio. The resulting scheme matches the best-known sampling methods for Ising models and is also validated on high-dimensional Gaussian mixtures. Its guarantees are tied to the analyzed structure and conditions.
neurips-2024-provable-posterior-sampling.tldr: Tilted transport uses linear inverse-problem structure to make posterior sampling provably easier, alongside a hardness result for generic denoising-based approaches.

paragraphs: Automated reasoning about algebraic inequalities faces a large space of possible reasoning steps and a shortage of high-quality training examples. AIPS addresses both issues by generating its own complex inequality theorems and learning to prove challenging problems without human demonstrations. Its target is Olympiad-level algebraic inequality reasoning.

The system combines a mixed reasoning approach to proof search with value curriculum learning on generated datasets. This links autonomous problem generation to improvement in proving performance. The generated material supplies training opportunities in a domain where the abstract identifies limited datasets as a major obstacle to existing machine learning methods.

On a test set of 20 problems at International Mathematical Olympiad level, AIPS solves 10 and outperforms the compared state-of-the-art methods. It also generates many non-trivial theorems, some judged by professional contestants to reach that level. One generated theorem was selected for a major city's 2024 Mathematical Olympiad. These results demonstrate both solving ability on the tested problems and the potential of autonomous theorem generation.
neurips-2024-proving-olympiad-algebraic-.tldr: AIPS generates its own inequality theorems and solves 10 of 20 Olympiad-level test problems without human demonstrations.

paragraphs: Vision transformers capture relationships between distant image patches, but ordinary self-attention becomes quadratically more expensive as the number of patches grows. Linear attention reduces that burden, though earlier approaches can lose effectiveness. QT-ViT aims to improve the balance between computational efficiency and predictive performance through a different approximation of attention.

The method replaces softmax-based attention with a second-order Taylor expansion. It then uses a fast approximation algorithm to reduce the computational cost of evaluating that quadratic expression. The design seeks to retain the useful properties of the richer expansion while enabling fast inference through a linear approximation.

The authors report that training does not require knowledge distillation or high-order attention residuals used in earlier linear-attention work. Their experiments show QT-ViT consistently outperforming EfficientViT models across different model sizes and establishing a new accuracy-speed Pareto frontier in the comparisons. The reported improvement is therefore about achievable tradeoffs: the proposed attention design supports a better combination of accuracy and speed in the evaluated models.
neurips-2024-qt-vit-improving-linear-att.tldr: QT-ViT combines a quadratic Taylor approximation of attention with fast computation to improve the measured accuracy-speed tradeoff.

paragraphs: Training a neural network on documents one after another can cause catastrophic interference, where learning later material harms performance on earlier material. This paper examines that behavior in a deliberately structured setting. Documents recur cyclically in a fixed order, so the training sequence contains a repeating pattern rather than independently sampled examples.

In this setting, the authors find an unexpected behavior in sequentially finetuned language models: performance on a previously seen document can recover before that document appears again. They describe this as anticipatory recovery from forgetting. The key observation concerns the timing of recovery relative to the document's next presentation in the cycle.

The behavior emerges and becomes more robust as models increase in parameter count. Experiments and visualizations explore these training dynamics in over-parameterized networks. The finding shows that forgetting and recovery can interact with repeated structure in the training environment in surprising ways. Its demonstrated setting is the fixed, recurring document sequence, which is central to interpreting the reported anticipation.
neurips-2024-reawakening-knowledge-antic.tldr: Language models trained on a fixed repeating document sequence can recover forgotten performance before the relevant document returns.

paragraphs: Selecting only part of an incoming data stream can reduce the expense of training image and text classifiers. However, selecting informative examples does not automatically protect every class. Existing batch-selection methods can struggle with class imbalance and distribution shifts, leaving the worst-performing class with poor generalization even when training is more economical.

REDUCR addresses this problem through class-aware priority weights. An online learning algorithm assigns priorities to data points with their class information in mind, guiding which examples are retained for training. The objective is to reduce the data used while preserving performance on the class that generalizes least well.

Experiments on vision and text classification tasks demonstrate both data efficiency and robust performance. On web-scraped datasets with imbalanced classes, the authors report improvements in worst-class and average test accuracy, with gains of around 15% over state-of-the-art methods. These findings support incorporating class priorities into data selection when reducing training cost would otherwise risk uneven performance across categories.
neurips-2024-reducr-robust-data-downsamp.tldr: REDUCR selects training data using class-aware priorities to reduce training cost while protecting worst-class generalization.

paragraphs: Some sequential decision problems contain hidden information that is chosen at the start and stays fixed throughout the interaction. Latent Markov Decision Processes model this situation. Earlier learning algorithms achieved guarantees under various structural assumptions, but a general algorithm matching the known sample-complexity lower bound had remained unavailable.

This paper introduces a sample-efficient algorithm for general latent MDPs without additional structural assumptions. The analysis develops a new off-policy evaluation lemma and a new coverage coefficient. These tools connect what can be inferred about policies from collected experience with the exploration needed when part of the environment is hidden.

Using those tools, the authors establish near-optimal guarantees for an optimistic exploration algorithm, effectively resolving the stated gap with existing lower bounds. The significance is a guarantee on the amount of interaction needed to learn in the general latent-MDP setting. The authors also suggest that this analytical perspective may help with other interactive learning problems, particularly partially observed environments, while presenting that broader relevance as a possibility.
neurips-2024-rl-in-latent-mdps-is-tracta.tldr: New off-policy evaluation and coverage tools yield near-optimal exploration guarantees for latent MDPs without additional structural assumptions.

paragraphs: Transferring knowledge from strong two-dimensional foundation models can improve three-dimensional scene understanding. Two obstacles remain: the representations in the two settings may not align well, and 3D datasets often contain unevenly represented groups. This paper addresses both problems within a framework for learning 3D representations through knowledge distillation.

A SAM-guided tokenization method replaces traditional nearest-neighbor-based tokenization, aligning the structure of a 3D transformer with region-level knowledge transfer. A group-balanced reweighting strategy addresses the long-tail distribution during distillation. Together, these changes target how the transferred information is organized and how strongly different groups contribute to learning.

The framework also uses two-stage masked token prediction. Teacher models trained in the first stage provide both global embeddings and local token embeddings for a student to predict. Evaluations cover 3D object detection and semantic segmentation on SUN RGB-D, ScanNet, and S3DIS. The authors report significant improvements over the compared state-of-the-art self-supervised methods, supporting the combination of aligned tokenization, balanced distillation, and prediction at global and local scales.
neurips-2024-sam-guided-masked-token-pre.tldr: SAM-guided tokenization, balanced knowledge transfer, and masked embedding prediction improve self-supervised 3D scene understanding.

paragraphs: Selling one item to several self-interested bidders can involve two different goals: maximizing welfare or maximizing the seller's revenue. Optimal auction designs may be impractical, particularly when bidders arrive sequentially. Posted pricing offers a practical alternative by setting fixed prices for different bidders rather than relying on a more elaborate auction procedure.

This paper asks how much information is needed to learn good posted prices. The information comes as samples from the distributions of bidders' values, and the target is pricing that is close to optimal. The authors consider both independent bidder values and correlated values, separately addressing welfare and revenue objectives.

For every setting studied, the paper provides upper and lower bounds on the required number of samples that match up to logarithmic factors. Upper bounds establish that sufficiently good prices can be learned with a certain amount of data; lower bounds show why substantially less data cannot generally suffice. Together, they characterize the statistical demands of learning posted prices across these different economic settings.
neurips-2024-sample-complexity-of-posted.tldr: The paper establishes nearly matching sample requirements for learning near-optimal posted prices under welfare and revenue objectives.

paragraphs: Meta learning seeks to support fast adaptation across tasks, making robustness across the task distribution an important concern. Tail-task risk minimization focuses attention on tasks associated with high risk. This paper develops the theoretical understanding of that strategy and introduces practical enhancements intended to improve robustness during adaptation.

The authors express the distributionally robust strategy as a max-min optimization problem and use a Stackelberg equilibrium as the solution concept. This frames the optimization through an ordered interaction between competing objectives. They also estimate a convergence rate, providing a way to characterize how the optimization approaches its proposed solution.

For the setting with tail risk, the paper derives a generalization bound and connects the analysis to estimated quantiles, which identify positions within a risk distribution. These results inform improvements to the studied strategy. Extensive evaluations demonstrate gains in robustness. The contribution combines an account of the optimization problem, analysis of generalization under tail risk, and empirical evidence for the resulting practical changes.
neurips-2024-theoretical-investigations-.tldr: The paper strengthens tail-task risk minimization in meta learning with optimization theory, generalization analysis, and practical robustness improvements.

paragraphs: Comparing vision-language models is difficult when many benchmarks require separate implementations and measure different capabilities. UniBench brings more than 50 benchmarks into one evaluation framework, organizing them around capabilities such as object recognition, spatial awareness, and counting. This makes it easier to examine what different forms of model progress actually improve.

The authors compare 59 publicly available models, including models trained on as many as 12.8 billion samples. Larger models and more training data improve many capabilities, but provide little benefit for reasoning or relations in the evaluations. Even leading models struggle with simple digit recognition and counting tasks that much simpler networks can solve.

The findings point toward data quality and tailored learning objectives as more promising interventions where scaling falls short. UniBench also offers model-selection guidance and a smaller representative benchmark set that runs in five minutes on one GPU. The practical message is that application-relevant capabilities deserve direct measurement, because improvements from scale are uneven across the abilities tested.
neurips-2024-unibench-visual-reasoning-r.tldr: UniBench compares 59 vision-language models and finds that scaling improves many abilities but offers little help for tested reasoning and relation tasks.
